auth.description: Klaviyo private API key for one account. Travels as the whole Authorization header behind Klaviyo's own scheme word. Keys are scoped per key: one minted without the scopes the shipped operations need will authenticate, pass verification, and fail on exactly the call that needs the missing scope
auth.name: klaviyo.api_key
auth.subject: unstated

config.help: Create one in Klaviyo under Settings > Account > API keys > Create Private API Key. Grant it these scopes and no more: accounts:read (for the connection test), profiles:read, profiles:write, lists:read and events:write. A key missing one of these still connects successfully and then fails on the single call that needs it. The key begins pk_ followed by a long hex string; it is shown once, so store it when it is created
config.label: Klaviyo private API key
config.name: api_key

description: Klaviyo marketing platform: read the account a key belongs to, read and create customer profiles, read lists, and post an event that can trigger a flow. Every request carries a dated API revision the vendor requires

operations.description: Read the Klaviyo account this API key belongs to, with its timezone, currency, industry and contact details. Returns exactly one account — a private key is scoped to one — so this is the call that answers 'which account am I connected to'. Also this connector's verify: it takes no argument and needs only the accounts:read scope

data.description: Always exactly one account: a private API key belongs to one account and cannot see another

contact_information.description: The sender identity and postal address Klaviyo puts in email footers: `default_sender_name`, `default_sender_email`, `organization_name`, `website_url`, and a `street_address` object (`address1`, `address2`, `city`, `region`, `country`, `zip`). Left untyped below the first level rather than enumerated in full

industry.description: The industry the account selected at signup

preferred_currency.description: ISO 4217 code the account reports revenue in. This is what an event's `value_currency` should normally match

public_api_key.description: The six-character public site id, repeated from `id`. Public by design — it is embedded in the account's own web pages

test_account.description: Whether this is a test account. A test account still accepts events and still runs flows

timezone.description: The account's IANA timezone. Klaviyo renders every date in the UI in this zone, while the API returns UTC

id.description: The account id, which is also Klaviyo's public (site) API key for this account — a browser-side identifier, not a secret

links.description: `{self}` — the JSON:API link to this resource
JSON:API document links. `next` is absent here; an account list is never paginated

operations.description: List customer profiles in the account, newest first. Returns the FIRST PAGE ONLY — Klaviyo pages with an opaque `page[cursor]` query parameter this connector cannot send, so there is no way to reach later pages and no way to filter. Every profile carries personal data: an email address, often a phone number and a postal location

data.description: One entry per profile, first page only

created.description: When the profile was first seen, in UTC

email.description: The profile's email address, or null. Personal data

external_id.description: The id this profile carries in the customer's own system, when one was supplied

last_event_date.description: When this profile last did anything Klaviyo recorded — the closest thing to an activity signal here

location.description: `address1`, `address2`, `city`, `region`, `zip`, `country`, `timezone`, `ip`, and `latitude`/`longitude` which Klaviyo returns as either numbers or strings. Personal data, including a home address where one was collected

phone_number.description: E.164 phone number, or null. Personal data

predictive_analytics.description: Klaviyo's modelled figures (historic and predicted CLV, churn probability, expected date of next order). Present only on accounts with enough order history

properties.description: Custom properties the account itself defined. Keys are chosen by whoever built the integration and are not knowable at build time; treat every value as potentially personal

subscriptions.description: Consent state per channel — `email.marketing`, `sms.marketing`, `sms.transactional` — each with a `consent` value and timestamps. This connector reports it and never interprets it: deciding who may be contacted needs more than this shape

id.description: The profile's Klaviyo id — what klaviyo-profile-get addresses it by

relationships.description: JSON:API relationship links for `lists`, `segments`, `push-tokens` and `conversations`. Only links: this connector sends no `include`, so nothing is expanded

links.description: `self`, and `next`/`prev` when more pages exist. **`next` is unusable here** — following it needs the `page[cursor]` query parameter (C-30)

operations.description: Read one customer profile by its Klaviyo id, with its identifiers, custom properties, consent state and location. Returns personal data about a named individual

params.description: The profile's Klaviyo id, from klaviyo-profile-list's `id` or from klaviyo-profile-create's response. Not an email address — Klaviyo addresses a profile by id here, and looking one up by email needs the `filter` query parameter this connector cannot send
params.name: id

email.description: The profile's email address, or null. Personal data

external_id.description: The id this profile carries in the customer's own system

location.description: Postal and network location — see klaviyo-profile-list for the field list. Personal data

phone_number.description: E.164 phone number, or null. Personal data

predictive_analytics.description: Modelled CLV and churn figures, when the account has enough history

properties.description: Account-defined custom properties; keys are not knowable at build time

subscriptions.description: Per-channel consent state. Reported, never interpreted

id.description: The profile's Klaviyo id, echoed back

relationships.description: Relationship links only; nothing is expanded

operations.description: Create a customer profile. At least one identifier is required — email, phone number or external id — and Klaviyo answers 409 Conflict if a profile with that identifier already exists, so this creates and never updates. The created profile can be marketed to only once it is subscribed, which this connector does not do

params.description: The profile's email address. Not required by Klaviyo on its own, but at least one of email, phone_number or external_id must be supplied or the call is rejected. Personal data about a named individual
params.name: email

params.description: Phone number in E.164 form, e.g. +15005550006. Klaviyo rejects other formats. Counts as an identifier
params.name: phone_number

params.description: The id this person carries in the calling system — an order-system customer id, say. Counts as an identifier, and is the one that lets a later call find this profile without holding an email address
params.name: external_id

params.description: Given name, as it should appear in a message greeting
params.name: first_name

params.description: The company this person belongs to
params.name: organization

created.description: When Klaviyo created the profile, in UTC

email.description: Echoes the address that was sent

last_event_date.description: Null on a profile just created: it has done nothing yet

location.description: Empty on a profile created by this operation, which sends no location

properties.description: Empty unless the account has default properties

subscriptions.description: **Not subscribed.** Creating a profile grants no marketing consent; the subscription endpoints this connector does not ship are what change this

id.description: The created profile's id — what klaviyo-profile-get reads back, and the only handle on it

operations.description: List the account's lists — static, opt-in collections of profiles, as opposed to segments, which are live queries and are not shipped here. Returns the FIRST PAGE ONLY; Klaviyo's `page[cursor]` query parameter cannot be sent by this connector. Returns the lists themselves, not their members

data.description: One entry per list, first page only

name.description: The list's name, as the account's marketers see it

opt_in_process.description: How a profile joins: `single_opt_in`, or `double_opt_in` where Klaviyo sends a confirmation message first. A flow that adds members has to respect this, and this connector does not add members

id.description: The list's id, a six-character code. This is what Klaviyo's own UI shows in a list URL

relationships.description: Relationship links for `profiles`, `tags` and `flow-triggers`. Links only — nothing is expanded, and the profiles endpoint behind the first is deliberately not shipped

links.description: `self`, plus `next`/`prev` when more pages exist. `next` is unusable here (C-30)

operations.description: Post an event about a customer — a purchase, a page view, anything the account measures. THIS CAN CAUSE A MESSAGE TO BE SENT: an event triggers any Klaviyo flow built on its metric, so an email or SMS may reach the named profile immediately. Klaviyo creates the metric and the profile on first use if they do not exist. Answers 202 Accepted with no body: the event is queued, not confirmed. Pass unique_id to make a retry safe — Klaviyo records only the first event with a given unique_id for the same profile and metric

params.description: What happened, as the account's marketers name it — `Placed Order`, `Viewed Product`. Klaviyo creates the metric on first use, so a typo silently creates a second metric nobody has built a flow on rather than failing
params.name: metric_name

params.description: The email address of the person this event is about. Klaviyo matches an existing profile on it and creates one if there is none, so an address typed wrongly creates a new profile rather than failing. Personal data
params.name: profile_email

params.description: The event's own detail, as a JSON object — order id, product names, values. Keys are whatever the account's flows and reports expect; Klaviyo imposes no shape. Pass an empty object when there is nothing to say
params.name: properties

params.description: The monetary value of the event, as a number, for revenue reporting. Omit it on an event that is not worth money
params.name: value

params.description: ISO 4217 code for `value`, e.g. EUR. Klaviyo converts to the account's preferred currency; omitting it means the account's own currency is assumed
params.name: value_currency

params.description: A caller-chosen id that makes this event's delivery safe to retry: Klaviyo records only the first event with a given unique_id for the same profile and metric. Omitting it means a retry posts a second event and may trigger a second message
params.name: unique_id
